source.title: The Multiple Realizability of Sentience in Living Systems and Beyond

confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed theoretical review in eNeuro from authors with standing in the basal-cognition literature, and it directly defines the substrate-independence concept ARC-089 relies on -- which supports the claim's coherence. But the same paper states the objection that bears hardest on ARC-089's practical purpose: there is no method to directly measure whether a substrate realises a mental function, only behavioural correlates. Since ARC-089 exists specifically to let a FUTURE substrate be evaluated on whether it INSTANTIATES the primitives rather than merely executes them, an epistemic argument that instantiation is not directly measurable cuts at the claim's operational value. Mixed, and confidence held mid-range because the paper is conceptual rather than empirical.
failure_signatures: The measurement problem: the paper states there are no available methods to directly measure mental states, so any substrate evaluation must proceed from behavioural correlates -- which cannot in principle distinguish a substrate that INSTANTIATES the cognifold primitives from one that merely SIMULATES their behavioural signature, and that distinction is the whole content of ARC-089.

Recognition failure across scales: the paper argues humans poorly recognise intelligence in unfamiliar problem spaces or at unfamiliar spatial/temporal scales, so a human-authored primitive vocabulary risks encoding the authors' substrate intuitions as if they were substrate-neutral criteria.

The minimal conditions for realising a cognitive function are stated as unresolved, so a compass claiming to evaluate future substrates against a fixed nine-primitive list asserts a specificity the multiple-realizability literature does not currently support.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Cognitive functions including sentience are multiply realizable and substrate-independent -- a function is substrate-independent if it can be achieved without contingency on a specific structure, material or medium -- but there is no method to directly measure mental states, only to infer them from behavioural correlates, and the minimal conditions for realisation remain unknown.
mapping.ree_translation: The first half underwrites ARC-089's premise: it is legitimate to specify cognifold function in hardware-neutral terms and expect that specification to be realisable in more than one medium. The second half constrains what ARC-089 can deliver: the claim promises a compass by which a future substrate is judged on whether it can INSTANTIATE the primitives, and this paper argues that instantiation is not directly observable, so the compass can only ever read behavioural proxies.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper is about sentience, not about REE's cognifold, and ARC-089 makes no sentience claim -- so the transfer is from a stronger and more contested target (phenomenal experience) to a weaker one (dynamical organisation). The measurement objection may therefore bite less hard on ARC-089 than on the paper's own subject: whether a device exhibits history-dependent deformation or multi-timescale field dynamics IS physically measurable, even if whether it feels anything is not. This entry should not be read as establishing that ARC-089's primitives are unmeasurable -- only that the subset which is functionally rather than physically specified (commitment as a real boundary, residue as action-landscape deformation) inherits the problem.
mapping.source_context: Theoretical review spanning basal cognition, non-neural and non-biological systems; no new empirical data.

confidence_components.notes: source_quality reflects a peer-reviewed but explicitly speculative review with no new data. transfer_risk elevated because the paper's target is sentience while ARC-089's is dynamical organisation -- the objection transfers only partially, and saying which part is exactly the work the mapping_caveat does.
